Subject: Redwood discovery recap + benchmark plan

Hi Sam / Leah —

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the infra and model ops folks. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

- Key pain: unpredictable tail latency on current hyperscaler endpoints (p95/p99 spikes during business hours) and high per-token costs when serving many short requests.
- Primary goal: validate whether Redwood can meet p95 < 150ms and p99 < 350ms for your 32-token avg workflows while improving tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens.
- Hyperscaler baseline you shared: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 480ms, tokens/sec ~ 1,200 for your test harness (batch size 8).

Proposal (attachments): we run a controlled A/B benchmark across your test harness comparing Redwood dedicated endpoints vs your hyperscaler baseline. Deliverables: CSV with raw latencies, PDF summary with p95/p99 and tokens/sec, and a short MA plan if results look good.

Next steps:
1) If you approve, we run the A/B test Tuesday (8/25) through Thursday (8/27).
2) We'll share raw CSV + summary by EOD Friday (8/28).
3) Follow-up call Monday to review results and discuss rollout options.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks.csv (stub), ma_step_plan.xlsx (stub)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. We're good to run the A/B test. A couple of clarifications before you start:

- Can you confirm the exact query distribution you'll use? Our production mix is ~65% short prompts (avg 32 tokens), 25% medium (avg 128 tokens), 10% long (avg 512 tokens).
- For the hyperscaler baseline I mentioned, those numbers were using batch size 8 and your current tokenization. If you can reproduce those conditions for a fair A/B, that'd be ideal.
- For success criteria, our EM wants p95 at or below 150ms and p99 at or below 350ms for the short prompt workload. Also include tokens/sec and cost delta per 1M tokens.

We can give you access to the test harness creds by EOD — copying infra.

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood discovery recap + benchmark plan — A/B results (summary)

Sam / Leah —

We completed the A/B run against the harness you shared. High-level summary below; full raw output attached (CSV) and a two-page PDF with charts attached.

Short-prompt workload (32 tokens avg, batch size 8) — production-like distribution replicated:
- Hyperscaler (baseline): p95 = 224 ms, p99 = 487 ms, tokens/sec = 1,210, cost per 1M tokens = $42
- Redwood Dedicated (our config: g-pool-2, quantized 4-bit, auto-batching): p95 = 138 ms, p99 = 312 ms, tokens/sec = 1,950, cost per 1M tokens = $27

Medium-prompt workload (128 tokens avg):
- Hyperscaler: p95 = 540 ms, p99 = 1,120 ms, tokens/sec = 820
- Redwood: p95 = 260 ms, p99 = 540 ms, tokens/sec = 1,350

Long-prompt workload (512 tokens avg):
- Hyperscaler: p95 = 1,950 ms, p99 = 3,400 ms, tokens/sec = 420
- Redwood: p95 = 1,120 ms, p99 = 1,950 ms, tokens/sec = 610

Notes:
- We saw consistent p95/p99 improvements across all buckets, biggest wins on short prompts (where KV cache + batching benefits compound).
- Tokens/sec is a steady-state measurement (after warmup) over 10-minute windows; raw CSV includes time-series windows for p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Cost estimate includes GPU utilization and network egress assumptions provided by Globex infra; we used your provided rates.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks.csv (raw), abtest_latency_p95_p99.pdf (summary)

Recommended next steps:
1) Pilot Redwood Dedicated in one region for 2 weeks with canary traffic (5–10% of live requests).
2) Run a production-shaped load test during a mid-week window to validate tail behavior under business-hour spikes.
3) If pilot hits our p95/p99 SLOs, we propose a phased rollout + MA/POC contract (see attached MA plan).

Scheduling: available Mon/Tue next week for a result review.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood discovery recap + benchmark plan — proposed pilot config

Hi team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Marissa — the numbers look promising. Proposed pilot configuration and test gating from infra/ops perspective:

- Pilot cluster: dedicated g-pool-2 in us-west-2 with KV cache enabled, 4-bit quantization.
- Traffic routing: start with 5% of short-prompt traffic (weighted by user id) for 3 days, then 10% for next 4 days if p95/p99 < target.
- Monitoring: we'll push dashboards for p50/p90/p95/p99, cost burn, and error rates. Alert if p99 increases >40% vs baseline for two consecutive 10-min windows.
- Failover: automatic fallback to hyperscaler variant if latency spike detected.

Action items for Globex infra: provide canary routing key (header or cookie) and a 1-hour maintenance window to run the production-shaped load test.

I added a short MA plan to the HubSpot deal for procurement. Link below.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
